assessments.reasoning: Nine contiguous captures cover all 132,314 bytes of the SPDX json/details record. Part 1 gives isDeprecatedLicenseId=false. Part 5 gives licenseId=GPL-3.0-or-later, the name “GNU General Public License v3.0 or later”, the comments and the matching header. The references cite GNU’s gpl-3.0-standalone.html and OSI’s /license/GPL-3.0. The shorter OSI URL does not change the explicit SPDX identifier.

The captured SPDX annotated tag v3.29.0 targets an object of type commit with SHA 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. This matches the or-later record’s exact revision. GitHub reports the tag as unsigned. The tag and generated record share the SPDX release lineage.

In the pinned GNU text, §14 in part 2 states the conditional right to follow a later FSF-published version. The sample notice in part 3 expressly offers that choice beginning with version 3. These passages support the meaning of the grant. The shared wording in SPDX’s rendition derives from the license and adds no independent corroboration of FSF authorship.

challenge.method: I checked the proposed election against the version-3-only header and two alternative §14 cases: a program specifying no version number and a program delegating future-version decisions to a proxy.
challenge.results: The only header ends at version 3. An unnumbered GPL grant permits any version ever published by the FSF, and a proxy provision depends on the proxy’s public acceptance. Neither alternative establishes the specific version-3-or-later notice in this claim. The FSF example and SPDX’s or-later header both express the recipient’s election directly.

limitations: The election applies where the relevant notice grants it. A shared GPLv3 heading, an SPDX template or a notice in another file cannot establish project-wide coverage or additional permissions.

The exact identifier belongs to SPDX. The FSF supplies the license terms, and “active” remains an Index editorial designation. The cross-referenced GNU HTML and OSI pages were not separately inspected.
reasoning: SPDX License List 3.29.0 lists GPL-3.0-or-later. Its standard header and the FSF application example both say “either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.” Section 14 identifies the eligible later versions as those published by the Free Software Foundation. SPDX’s comment says “some later version”, while its header says “any later version”. The former describes the version a recipient may choose and the latter describes the available choice.
